pairs.difference: A (planet): the whole sphere and ring share one even, glassless plastic finish. There is no surface grain and no gloss variation between the body, the stripe and the ring, and the ring is a flat cream band with no edge or seam detail. B (fins): the matte rubber foot pockets read differently from the glossy yellow blades, and the dark inserts are a third finish. That mix of finishes matches the real cards.
pairs.fix: Make the planet's body a soft satin finish with faint, fine banding streaks inside the orange. Give the ring a slightly glossier hard-plastic edge with a thin highlighted lip, so the ring and the sphere don't read as the same material.

pairs.difference: A: the target has matte painted rings, the bear is soft felt-like plush with a satin bow, and the wood frame has fine grain. B: the ice tray is glossy pink plastic with a frosty speckle along its edges, and the ice cubes are translucent with small bubbles. Both cards mix finishes and keep their fine detail small, the way the real cards do. Nothing on my vector separates them.

A (rocket): the silver body is covered in long, even brushed-metal streaks that look like an overlaid texture, not form shading. The red fins and nose are the same smooth lacquer as the porthole ring. B (submarine): glossy yellow hull, small rivets at the right scale, and the copper porthole rims are a different finish from the hull. That is closer to the real anchor and lamp.
pairs.fix: Paint the rocket body as smooth, softly shaded silver with one broad highlight and no brushed streak texture. Make the red fins a slightly duller painted metal than the glossy nose cone.

pairs.difference: A (robot): the white body is a hard, crisp, evenly bright plastic with a very high highlight share, and it stands on a riveted, brushed-steel floor whose sharp anisotropic streaks don't match the soft rendering of the real cards. B (boxing gloves): soft, slightly blurred red leather with fine crease lines at the cuff. That matches the softness of the real computer and the real glove lesson.
pairs.fix: Soften the robot's white plastic to an off-white satin with gentle falloff, not a bright, uniform sheen. Replace the brushed, riveted metal floor with a plain, soft-shaded floor that has no streak texture.

pairs.difference: B is the real computer card from the lessons: soft, slightly blurred beige plastic and a dark matte screen. A (alien): the green body is a uniform glossy vinyl, and the pink spots and eye rims all share one lacquer. It stands on the same brushed, riveted metal floor seen on the p04 robot, with crisp streaks and screw heads.
pairs.fix: Give the alien a soft, slightly matte rubbery skin with a faint, fine surface grain, and keep glossy highlights only on the eyes. Replace the brushed, riveted steel floor with a plain soft-shaded surface.

pairs.difference: A: the slide is smooth glossy green plastic, the deck is wood with fine plank grain, and the pool tiles are crisp. B: the beach ball is glossy vinyl with a soft gradient and a matte purple cap, on sand with fine speckle. B's metrics fall low, but its softness looks like the real computer card's, not like a generator artifact. I see no clear tell on either card.

A (bus): soft, slightly blurry red paint, simple windows, and little micro-detail. That matches the real cards' softness. B (pod): crisp silver metal with many tiny rivets, panel seams and hinge plates, a ring of glowing bulbs, and a sharply reflective glass door showing the seat inside. This is the dense, sharp fine detail the generated lesson cards add.
pairs.fix: Simplify the pod's metal shell: drop most of the rivets and panel seams, keep one soft broad highlight, and make the door glass a smooth teal with a single soft reflection, without a detailed interior.

pairs.difference: A (vending machine): glossy blue body, condensation droplets on the glass, and soft cans behind it. The texture stays fine and the finishes vary. B (control panel): one uniform satin-grey metal box with crisp screws at the corners, sharp chrome rings around the buttons, and a brushed steel table with long streaks. The added fasteners and brushed streaks match the generated lessons.
pairs.fix: Make the console's body a soft painted metal with gentle shading, with no screws or side panel plate. Keep the red buttons glossy, and replace the brushed steel tabletop with a plain soft surface.

pairs.difference: A (scout jacket): matte, soft fabric with seams, pocket flaps and a button, a felt sash, and enamel-like glossy badges. Several finishes in one object, like the real sleeping bag. B (helmet): the white shell is one smooth lacquer, the gold visor is a big, very saturated glossy plane, and the evenly spaced bolts on the collar are the same plastic. The surface is uniform with little material contrast.
pairs.fix: Give the helmet's white shell a slightly matte, painted finish with a faint seam line, keep the visor glossy but less saturated with one soft reflection, and make the collar ring a duller metal.

pairs.difference: A (rover): crisp, CG-like white panels with many small screws, vent slits and lined seat cushions, sharply cut tire treads, and a crater floor full of fine pebbles. The detail is dense and sharp. B (boat): soft painted wood with quiet plank lines, a chunky rope and water ripples, rendered softly like the real signpost.
pairs.fix: Simplify the rover: remove most of the screws and vent slits, render the white body as soft satin plastic with rounded edges, give the tires plain soft treads, and smooth the ground into soft, low-contrast dust.

pairs.difference: A (music player): soft matte-satin orange plastic, glossy white earbuds and small coloured LEDs. The finishes vary and the edges are soft. B (UFO): the silver saucer has a fine brushed/noisy grain across its top, the glass dome is very glossy with sharp streak reflections, and the orange bulbs are identical glossy beads. The metal grain is a generated tell.
pairs.fix: Make the saucer smooth silver with soft shading and no brushed grain, and give the dome one soft highlight instead of sharp streaks.

pairs.difference: A (space station): detail is above the real range. Every solar panel carries a fine grid of cells, the hull has many tiny panel lines, plates and rivets, and the starfield is sharp and grainy. B (pool bar): faceted pineapple, glossy grapes, a matte concrete counter and straw roof. The finishes vary and the detail stays reasonably soft.
pairs.fix: Draw the solar panels as plain glossy blue with only a few divider lines and no fine cell grid. Make the hull smooth off-white with one or two seams and no rivets, and soften the stars.

pattern: Generated cards give themselves away at close range by adding crisp micro-detail the real cards don't carry: rivets, screws, panel seams, vent slits, fine solar-cell grids and brushed-metal streak textures, often on a riveted steel floor. They also put one uniform lacquer finish over the whole object. Real cards are softer and slightly blurred at 2×, keep fine marks small and sparse, and mix matte and glossy parts within one object.
